title: Spatial correlations of photons interacting via transverse Rydberg blockade
authors: Bankim Chandra Das, Daniil Svirskiy, Matthias Metternich, Wolfgang Alt, Sebastian Hofferberth, Ofer Firstenberg
abstract: We develop a theory of the transverse spatial dynamics of two interacting photons in a Rydberg nonlinear medium. Extending the well-studied one-dimensional case, we explore both longitudinal and transverse correlations of photons propagating as Rydberg polaritons. We identify distinct behaviors and scaling laws for these correlations, arising from fundamentally different mechanisms in the two directions: diffraction for transverse correlations and diffusion for longitudinal correlations. We develop a model incorporating a Gaussian optical beam and an inhomogeneous atomic density distribution, from which we derive quantitative predictions for correlation functions in both directions. We further show that the propagation equations can be reduced to a single Schrödinger-like equation, allowing approximate solutions that are supported by full numerical results. Our findings indicate that the transverse correlation length is determined primarily by the blockade radius, whereas the longitudinal correlation length is limited by bandwidth. These results establish transverse Rydberg blockade as a distinct and measurable correlation mechanism and show that spatial photon correlations provide a direct means of measuring the blockade radius.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates how two photons interact via transverse Rydberg blockade in an EIT medium. It finds that the transverse correlation length is set by the blockade radius, while the longitudinal correlation is limited by bandwidth, demonstrating distinct physical mechanisms in each direction. The results provide a novel, measurable diagnostic tool for characterizing Rydberg interactions using spatial photon statistics.
main_problem: The paper develops a theory for the transverse spatial dynamics of two interacting photons propagating in a Rydberg nonlinear medium, extending beyond the standard one-dimensional analysis.
main_result: It establishes that transverse Rydberg blockade creates a distinct, measurable correlation mechanism whose length scale is determined by the blockade radius, independent of the EIT bandwidth.
method: The authors derive an effective two-photon Schrödinger-like equation and analyze its transport equation by separating the interaction potential into dissipative and dispersive parts.
model_or_system: The system involves two photons propagating through a medium containing atoms excited to Rydberg states under Electromagnetically Induced Transparency (EIT) conditions, modeled by a two-polariton Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Two-photon wavefunction, two-photon correlation functions, transverse and longitudinal correlation lengths, and the blockade width.
important_parameters: Blockade radius ($r_b$), EIT bandwidth, input beam waist ($w_0$), and optical depth (OD).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as the undepleted tail ($I \simeq 1$) and the separation of the interaction potential into dissipative and dispersive components.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup, the 4D configuration space, the stationary two-photon wavefunction showing blockade, and the final results comparing transverse (diffractive) and longitudinal (diffusive) correlation scaling.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from setting up the full two-polariton Hamiltonian to deriving an effective 2D Schrödinger equation. It then analyzes the anisotropy by treating the transverse and longitudinal kinetic terms separately, leading to distinct scaling laws for the correlation lengths.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for using spatial photon correlations to probe fundamental atomic interactions (Rydberg blockade) in a highly controllable quantum optical setting, bridging quantum optics and atomic physics.
